scenario: Scenario 4: Dehydration during a Mars mission
what_happens: Busy workday with exercise; Sarah drinks less than planned and sweats. Feels fine.
key_measurements: Fluid intake below 2.5 L/day target | Urine output low, urine dark | Weight below personal baseline | HR 76
charm_assessment: Negative fluid balance on top of the plasma volume already lost in weightlessness. Hydration warning, not a diagnosis.
checks_requested: Daily fluid balance (intake vs urine output); morning weight.
immediate_action_steps: Remind Sarah to drink; plan fluids around exercise.
equipment: C.H.A.R.M. tablet, drink log, scale (body mass device).

scenario: Scenario 4: Dehydration during a Mars mission
key_measurements: HR 76 | BP 116/74 | SpO2 99% | RR 15 | Shock index 0.66
charm_assessment: Vital signs close to Sarah's personal baseline. Fluid-intake trend already flagged.

scenario: Scenario 4: Dehydration during a Mars mission
charm_assessment: Heart rate rising against baseline while BP falls slightly: early compensation for lower blood volume. Suspected dehydration.
checks_requested: Repeat HR and BP; symptom questions; urine color and volume.
immediate_action_steps: Stop activity; rest; start oral rehydration solution (ORS) slowly if able to drink; repeat measurements.
equipment: BP cuff, wearable, ORS packets, potable water.

scenario: Scenario 4: Dehydration during a Mars mission
charm_assessment: Shock index above 1.0: the heart is working hard to hold blood pressure. Escalate to the Crew Medical Officer.
checks_requested: Repeat BP and HR; mental status; fluid intake and urine output since morning.
blood_lab_tests: Hemoglobin/hematocrit if an onboard analyzer exists (expect a rise from hemoconcentration).
immediate_action_steps: Notify Crew Medical Officer; keep Sarah resting and secured; continue ORS if alert and not vomiting.
equipment: BP monitor, pulse oximeter, onboard blood analyzer if available.

scenario: Scenario 4: Dehydration during a Mars mission
what_happens: Very dizzy and weak, cannot continue activity.
charm_assessment: Suspected significant hypovolemia or another cause of shock. Immediate medical assessment.
checks_requested: Continuous HR, BP, RR, SpO2; responsiveness.
blood_lab_tests: Hemoglobin/hematocrit, electrolytes and glucose if available.
immediate_action_steps: Crew Medical Officer to Sarah; ABC assessment; continuous monitoring; IV access if trained and the protocol requires.
equipment: ECG/vital-sign monitor, IV kit, IV fluid supply.
treatment_guidance: Isotonic IV fluid (e.g. normal saline 0.9%) per approved protocol. C.H.A.R.M. does not choose or dose fluids.

scenario: Scenario 4: Dehydration during a Mars mission
what_happens: Same picture can come from bleeding, infection or a heart rhythm problem.
key_measurements: Fever? Irregular pulse? Signs of bleeding? Hemoglobin falling instead of rising?
charm_assessment: C.H.A.R.M. does not assume dehydration: it lists the alternatives the crew must check.
checks_requested: Temperature; pulse regularity (ECG); look for bleeding.
blood_lab_tests: Hemoglobin trend: a fall suggests bleeding, a rise suggests dehydration.
immediate_action_steps: Follow the matching protocol if another cause is found.

scenario: Scenario 4: Dehydration during a Mars mission
what_happens: Mars communication delay; no real-time physician.
key_measurements: Live values continue streaming to C.H.A.R.M.
charm_assessment: C.H.A.R.M. keeps the onboard hypovolemia protocol and structured reassessment every few minutes.
immediate_action_steps: Open onboard emergency protocol; continue step-by-step guidance despite the delay.
equipment: C.H.A.R.M. tablet plus the same equipment.

scenario: Scenario 4: Dehydration during a Mars mission
charm_assessment: Improving but not yet stable. Continue fluids per protocol and repeat measurements.
checks_requested: Repeat full vitals every few minutes; urine output.
immediate_action_steps: Continue rest; document response; no return to activity yet.
treatment_guidance: Continue fluids until intake and urine output recover.

charm_assessment: Returning toward baseline, but the full fluid deficit is not corrected yet.
checks_requested: Repeat full vitals every few minutes; urine output.
immediate_action_steps: Continue rest; document response; no return to activity yet.
treatment_guidance: Continue fluids until intake and urine output recover.

scenario: Scenario 4: Dehydration during a Mars mission
key_measurements: Fluid intake back on target | Urine output normal | HR and BP at baseline | Weight back toward baseline
charm_assessment: Sustained return to baseline. Return to duty only after medical clearance.
checks_requested: Fluid balance and weight next morning.
immediate_action_steps: Gradual return to duty after clearance; adjust daily fluid plan for exercise days.
